proposition.claim:
An equationally noetherian family \(\mathcal G\) has the following uniform property: for every finitely generated \(G\), a finitely presented \(G_0\) admits an epimorphism \(\alpha:G_0\to G\) such that \(\alpha^*:\operatorname{Hom}(G,\Gamma)\to
\operatorname{Hom}(G_0,\Gamma)\) is bijective for every \(\Gamma\in\mathcal G\). With the fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter \(\omega\), the stable kernel is \[K_\omega=\{g:\phi_i(g)=1\ \text{for $\omega$-almost every }i\},
 \qquad L=G/K_\omega .\] Theorem 2.4 equates the family property with \(\omega\)-almost-sure factorization through this quotient. Its external proof is a declared input, rather than a result reproduced here.

The finite-index cyclic/Z^3/Z^2 semidirect Z groups in the five-geometries reduction all embed in SL(3,Z).

Spherical lens space L(241,1)=S3/<(z1,z2)->(zeta*z1,zeta*z2)>, zeta primitive241st root. C241 acts freely; quotient is closed geometric3-manifold with pi1=C241. 241 is prime and exceeds240, so no proper subgroup has index<=240.
